title: Grateful Dead Live at Euphoria Ballroom on 1970-07-14
source: SBD > Master Reel > Dat> cd> shn> cd> ?> shn

ai_review.summary: High‑fidelity soundboard capture of a stellar July 14 1970 show with a smoking Cosmic Charlie and rare acoustic gems, despite a few cuts.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers crisp, classic 70s soundboard quality that lets the band’s dynamics shine – from Jerry’s rich tone on New Speedway to the thunderous drums that drive China Cat → Jam → I Know You Rider.  Highlights include an exceptional Cosmic Charlie, a rare acoustic How Long Blues, and a soulful Uncle John’s Band, while the only real drawbacks are the missing opening of Easy Wind and a chopped Good Lovin' segment.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars, praising both performance (standout songs, rare acoustic set) and recording fidelity; only minor technical glitches are noted, yielding a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clean overall with classic 1970 soundboard warmth.  Some glitches, cuts (Easy Wind intro, Good Lovin'), and occasional tape hiccups, but the mix is balanced – drums are high and lively.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A relaxed acoustic set (rare How Long Blues, Deep Elem, Cumberland) segues into a more electric second half; the transition China Cat → Jam → I Know You Rider is praised for its funky percussion, though some slower Weir numbers dip the momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His classic guitar tone shines on New Speedway and How Long Blues; noted for rich body and occasional electric work on acoustic tunes.
band_member_comments.Phil: Long solo in Good Lovin' praised (though cut), drums‑solo interplay highlighted, high in the mix throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Only minor comment about slower ‘Cowboy’ Weir numbers; otherwise not specifically mentioned.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers are described as 'smoking', high in the mix, and delivering funky percussion on China Cat → Jam → I Know You Rider.
